title: The fruits of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22–23)
hookLine: the Latin Bible lists twelve: charity, joy, peace, patience and more (CCC 1832)

lines: THE WORKS OF THE FLESH, THEN THE FRUIT.
cards: Open a modern Bible to Galatians chapter five and count the fruit of the Spirit. Nine. Now open the Douay-Rheims to the same verse and count again.
Twelve. Nobody slipped in a few extra. The difference is centuries old, and it says something about how the Bible traveled.

Paul has just listed what he calls the works of the flesh: enmities, contentions, envy, anger, quarrels, drunkenness and more. Now he lists the opposite, and the Catholic Church still counts it the old way.

teach.h: TWELVE IN LATIN, NINE IN GREEK.
teach.b: Here it is in the Douay-Rheims: "But the fruit of the Spirit is, charity, joy, peace, patience, benignity, goodness, longanimity, mildness, faith, modesty, continency, chastity." Twelve.
The Greek text behind modern Bibles has nine. The old Latin Bible has twelve; some scholars think early translators rendered a few Greek words with two Latin ones.
The Catechism lists the twelve, and says that the tradition of the Church counts them so. Look at two words Paul chose.
First, works versus fruit. Works are things you make: you build them, you produce them. Fruit grows.
You can water a tree and prune it, but you can't force an apple. Paul's point is that these qualities are what the Spirit grows in a life given over to God. Second, fruit, not fruits.
In Paul's Greek it's singular, one fruit, the way one orange has many segments. Charity heads the list, and the others may be read as its flavors.
Today's line comes from Jesus in Matthew's Gospel, talking about telling true teachers from false: "By their fruits you shall know them."
A tree is known by what it bears. Catholics use the twelve as a kind of mirror. Not a checklist to grade yourself, but a way to notice what's already growing.

teach.h: BY THEIR FRUITS YOU SHALL KNOW THEM.
teach.b: And the list is very ordinary. Patience in traffic. Mildness on the phone.
Joy at a kitchen table. Nothing on it requires a miracle, just a life where something is quietly growing.

how: Catholics learn the twelve fruits of the Spirit as listed in the Catechism (1832), often in preparation for confirmation, alongside the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit.

o: fruit: what the Spirit grows, not what you make
the good works a Christian builds by effort
a harvest offering brought to the temple

games.q: inside the list — tap the pairs.

s: the Catholic Church added three fruits of its own
the twelve come from the old Latin Bible, which Catholic tradition kept.

games.q: you want to know whether a teacher is true. what does Jesus say to look at?
games.why: "by their fruits you shall know them": a tree is known by what it bears.

practice: Let the list pass slowly through your mind: charity, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, long patience, mildness, faith, modesty, self-control, chastity.

Don't grade yourself; just ask which one you've actually seen in yourself this week, even once, even small, and remember the scene. If you pray, thank God for what's growing; if not, notice it and be glad.

wordCard.voice: Karpos. The Greek word for fruit, singular: one fruit of the Spirit with many flavors, charity first among them. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: fruit. singular in Galatians 5:22, one fruit with many qualities.

carryVoice: Your line: by their fruits. And that's week eighty-three: enigma, where is thy sting, earthen vessels, skolops, a cheerful giver, all one, and the fruits of the Spirit. Until tomorrow.
